title: Cohomology comparison for the open complement of finitely many points
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field, let Cbar be a proper smooth connected curve over k [def-sc-curves], let S be a finite set of closed points of Cbar, let C := Cbar minus S, and let j:C \to Cbar be the open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. For the etale sheaf G_m [def-sc-gm-torsor] on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], the natural map H^q(Cbar_et,j_*G_m) \to H^q(C_et,G_m) is an isomorphism for every q <= 2.

source.place: Discussion preceding Tag 03RM (Theorem 59.68.5): stalks of R^q j_*G_m computed via the strict henselization, R^1 = 0 by Hilbert 90 and R^2 = 0 since the Brauer group of the fraction field of a strictly henselian DVR vanishes; then the low-degree Leray comparison

proof.text: For a geometric point x of Cbar lying in C, j is an isomorphism on an etale neighbourhood, so all higher direct-image stalks vanish. For x over a boundary point P in S, the stalk formula identifies (R^q j_* G_m)_x with H^q of the fraction field of the strict henselization of the DVR O_{Cbar,P}; q=1 vanishes by Hilbert 90 and q=2 vanishes because this field has zero Brauer group.

Apply the Leray spectral sequence for j to G_m. The vanishing of the R^1 and R^2 higher direct images from step 1 makes the edge map H^q(Cbar_et,j_*G_m) \to H^q(C_et,G_m) an isomorphism for q=0,1,2 by the low-degree Leray comparison.
